panel.runningFinalizeDescription: Available once the run is complete

actionArgCarriers.note: How a §2.5 action argument (`runId`, `generation`) reads out of the wire value that carried it. A JSON number that is an exact non-negative integer IS the identity it names, whichever carrier the sender minted it with: the shell's own action arguments build `generation` as a float (`UiValue::Number`), a guest mints it with `DslValue::uint`, and a targeted action's `runId` travels as text. A reader that accepts only some of these does not reject a wrong value, it silently misreads a right one — `generation` reading `None` is `toolRun.stale`, so EVERY finalize of EVERY app was refused, runs reached `complete` and stayed there, and a start against a live run is `toolRun.busy`. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END.

readOnlyRun.note: A run that declares `mutating: false` authors no provisional edit, so there is nothing for a finalize to publish and nothing for a user to review: its completion IS its finalization, applied in the same driver turn that completed the job. Leaving it parked in `complete` only holds the tool's single run slot open, and a start against a non-terminal run is `toolRun.busy` — which is how a read-only preview run could run exactly once per session. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END.

settingsReads.note: The toy run declares `settings.config = ["/selected"]` (its target). A config publication that republishes the same value and a window-config publication (a camera move) are not settings changes; a changed target is. A run that declares no settings reads is never reconfigured by any settings publication.

retarget.note: A job built through `build_retargetable_tool_run_job` stays resident while its run is complete and is retargeted in place: a raise and a lower reconfigure it without a rebuild (its resumedFrom counter stays 0), and a base change rebinds it to the next generation without a rebuild.

rebind.note: A base change during a run hands every later tick the new identity: a plain job is rebuilt under it from its checkpoint, a retargetable job is rebound in place; either way the run keeps appending after the rebase.

chord.note: A §2.5 action without any identity argument — what a keyboard chord dispatches — targets the instance's live run at its generation of this dispatch; an identity argument that is stale still no-ops.

compact.note: A retract followed by re-appends spread over several ticks keeps the previous overlay rendered until the job reaches its next checkpoint, so the renderer never shows a half re-appended overlay.

traceKeys.note: Every job of a run shares one trace key allocator: keys it hands out lie above every key the run's ticks upserted and every key allocated before.

boardLane.note: A board-2d scene surface carries the toolRunTrace lane exactly like a world-3d one: the spine names the lane and the paged carrier holds the delta.

windowSettingsReads.note: A run started from a window declares the window-config fields its jobs read per window kind: its job request carries that window's config snapshot, a publication on another window of the same kind or an unchanged value never reconfigures, and a changed value on the starting window does.

readerWindows.note: A run declares the window kinds whose bodies render its state (ToolRunDefinition.windows): every tick dirties them next to the panel and the scene windows, and their render reads the run's progress, steps and the latest tick payload through ArtifactView::tool_run().

concurrentReadOnly.note: Read-only runs run concurrently, one per (tool, window), each with its own run id, trace and panel group; a second mutating start while a mutating run is non-terminal is toolRun.busy; actions address a run by its runId; presence follows the mutating run, else the most recent run.
